classification.difficultyReason: Convert ordered pairs into arrows and check whether every codomain element receives exactly one arrow.

content.prompt: Draw a diagram to depict each of the following functions from $\{1,2,3\}$ to $\{1,2,3\}$, and determine if the functions are bijective.

answer.worked: The diagram shows $1\mapsto2$, $2\mapsto3$ and $3\mapsto1$. Each element of the codomain has exactly one preimage, so the function is both injective and surjective. Therefore, it is bijective.

answer.short: Not bijective: not injective and not surjective.
answer.worked: The diagram shows $1\mapsto3$, $2\mapsto1$ and $3\mapsto3$. Since $f(1)=f(3)=3$ but $1\ne3$, the function is not injective. The codomain element $2$ has no preimage, so the function is not surjective. Therefore, it is not bijective.
